# Psalm 96 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Sing a brand-new song to the LORD! Sing to the LORD, everyone on earth!

**2** Sing to the LORD and praise his name! Share the good news of his salvation every single day.

**3** Announce his glory to the nations, his amazing deeds to every people group.

**4** The LORD is great — he deserves the highest praise! He is more awe-inspiring than any other god.

**5** All the gods of the nations are just empty idols, but the LORD made the heavens!

**6** Splendor and majesty radiate from him; strength and beauty fill his sanctuary.

**7** Give the LORD credit, all you nations! Give the LORD the glory and the strength he deserves!

**8** Give the LORD the honor his name is worth! Bring your offering and enter his courtyards!

**9** Worship the LORD, dressed in the beauty of holiness! Tremble before him, all the earth!

**10** Tell the nations: 'The LORD is king!' The world stands firm and cannot be shaken. He will judge the peoples fairly.

**11** Let the heavens celebrate and the earth be glad! Let the sea and everything in it roar with praise!

**12** Let the fields and everything growing in them be ecstatic! Then all the trees in the forest will sing for joy —

**13** because the LORD is coming! He's coming to judge the earth! He will judge the world with righteousness and the nations with his truth.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **96:11-13**: The whole creation is invited to the party — heavens, earth, sea, fields, even the trees! In the Bible, God's judgment isn't something creation dreads. It's what creation has been waiting for, because it means everything will finally be set right.

- **96:5**: One devastating line: 'All the gods of the nations are just empty idols, but the LORD made the heavens.' That's the entire argument against idolatry in one sentence.

— PNEUMA
